identification.summary: GREYVIBE is a threat cluster named and tracked by WithSecure, described as a Russia-nexus group that uses generative AI and LLMs across its operations against Ukrainian targets [S1]. WithSecure rates it low-to-moderately sophisticated, citing operational security failures, design flaws in its malware and heavy LLM reliance, and says it lacked the sophistication and operational discipline typically associated with mature nation-state actors [S1][S2]. Its main Windows malware is the PowerShell-based LegionRelay and PhantomRelay, and it also uses Android spyware called FallSpy [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Activity dates to at least 2025-08; WithSecure first found the activity in 2026-01 [S2].
identification.notes: WithSecure tracks DroneLink separately and is still investigating its relationship to the wider GREYVIBE cluster, although DroneLink shares C2 infrastructure and post-compromise tooling with PrincessClub [S1]. One secondary write-up suggests possible overlap with the TrickBot ecosystem and UAC-0098; this was not confirmed against WithSecure's own text and is not adopted here [S1].

attribution.confidence: WithSecure assesses GREYVIBE as Russia-nexus/Russian-speaking and says its activity aligns with Russian state interests, but it has not identified definitive links to any previously tracked threat group and BleepingComputer reports researchers could not confidently classify it as a nation-state operation [S1][S2]. Confidence statements here are WithSecure's and the press's, not a government attribution.
attribution.basis: Russian-language malware panels and a command-and-control server set to Moscow time [S2]; targeting of Ukrainian military, government, civilian and business victims [S1].

objectives: Activity is assessed as consistent with intelligence gathering against Ukraine aligned with Kremlin interests, with no definitive state attribution [S1]. The malware steals files, screenshots, browser credentials and Telegram and WhatsApp data, and sets up RDP access [S1].

targeting.notes: Lures impersonate Zoom and LAPAS, adult-club sites and military charities [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: The group uses custom malware: LegionRelay and PhantomRelay (PowerShell RATs), the Android spyware FallSpy, and the custom obfuscators LOOKVALPS and DAYLIGHT [S1]. LegionRelay supports file theft, screenshots, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration and RDP setup, and WithSecure assesses it was likely developed with LLM assistance [S1]. Delivery uses spear-phishing, ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA pages and fake websites [S1][S2]. Post-compromise tools include WireGuard VPN and ZAPiXDESK [S1]. WithSecure reports use of ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Ideogram, for Ukrainian-language phishing content and imagery for fake sites [S2]. Design flaws in the malware gave WithSecure insight into victimology and operator behavior [S1].

campaigns.summary: WithSecure reports the campaign has run since at least August 2025 [S2].

campaigns.name: Discovery by WithSecure
campaigns.summary: WithSecure first found the activity in January 2026 [S2].

campaigns.name: PhantomClick
campaigns.summary: Fake CAPTCHA pages impersonating Zoom and LAPAS in ClickFix style deliver PhantomRelay [S1].

campaigns.name: PrincessClub
campaigns.summary: Fake Ukrainian adult-club websites deliver FallSpy on Android and PhantomRelayV1 or LegionRelay on Windows [S1].

campaigns.name: DroneLink
campaigns.summary: Sites posing as charitable foundations supporting the Ukrainian military deliver WireGuard alongside LegionRelay; they share C2 with PrincessClub and DAYLIGHT-obfuscated LegionRelay scripts, but WithSecure tracks DroneLink separately [S1].

campaigns.name: PhantomMail
campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing operation named in press coverage of the report [S2].

campaigns.name: Public reporting
campaigns.summary: WithSecure published its GREYVIBE report on 2026-05-28, with BleepingComputer coverage the same day [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: Russia-nexus, Russian-speaking cluster, low-to-moderate sophistication, no definitive link to a known group [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: LegionRelay, PhantomRelay, FallSpy, LOOKVALPS, DAYLIGHT, WireGuard, ZAPiXDESK, with LLM-assisted development and lures [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Shared C2 across PrincessClub and DroneLink, a Moscow-time C2 server and Russian-language malware panels, plus fake CAPTCHA, adult-club and charity websites [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Ukrainian military, government, civilian and business entities [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Ukraine war context; activity assessed as aligned with Russian state intelligence-gathering interests [S1].
diamond.technology: Windows (PowerShell), Android, Telegram/WhatsApp, RDP and browser credential stores; generative AI services used by the operator [S1][S2].

gaps: Could not open the WithSecure report, BleepingComputer, CSO or Hacker News pages directly (host unreachable from this environment); details rest on search-result summaries and should be checked against the primary WithSecure report and its IOCs.
No sponsor, government attribution or definitive link to a tracked group; the TrickBot/UAC-0098 overlap claim is unverified.
Relationship of DroneLink to the core cluster remains under WithSecure investigation.
Dates of individual campaigns, victim counts and detailed infrastructure are not established.
